title: Data
text:
Transfermarkt is the most comprehensive platform for tracking football player market values, updated regularly by a community of football analysts. Player-level market values for all Turkish Süper Lig clubs across the 2023-24, 2024-25, and 2025-26 seasons were retrieved via the worldfootballR R package.

Currency: Euro (€)
Coverage: All registered players per season (~400–500 players/season)
Key Variables: squad_name, player_name, player_position, player_market_value_euro




FBref provides detailed football statistics powered by StatsBomb data. Both club-level standings (W, D, L, GF, GA, GD, Pts) and player-level statistics (goals, assists, minutes played, position, goalkeeper save percentage) were collected here.

Coverage: 3 seasons, ~20 clubs/season, all registered players
Key Variables: Squad, W, D, L, GF, GA, GD, Pts, Player, Pos, Min, Gls, Ast, Save%




Capology.com aggregates club-level wage bill data. The worldfootballR function capology_club_wage_data() was used to retrieve Turkish Süper Lig clubs’ total annual wage expenditures.

Currency: Euro (€), annualised
Important: January (winter transfer window) arrivals have their annual wage halved before inclusion in team totals.
Coverage: Club-level total wage bill per season

title: Data
text:
Data Collection Code
The following code was used to collect raw data. Sys.sleep() delays are applied between requests to respect rate limits on Transfermarkt and FBref. Raw files are saved as .RData files in the data/ folder.


Package Setup
if (!requireNamespace("worldfootballR", quietly = TRUE)) install.packages("worldfootballR")
if (!requireNamespace("tidyverse",      quietly = TRUE)) install.packages("tidyverse")

library(worldfootballR)
library(dplyr)
library(purrr)
library(stringr)




Transfermarkt — Squad Market Values
collect_tm_values <- function(start_year) {
  message("Fetching Transfermarkt: ", start_year, "-", start_year + 1)
  Sys.sleep(8)
  tm_player_market_values(country_name = "Turkey", start_year = start_year)
}

tm_2324 <- collect_tm_values(2023); Sys.sleep(8)
tm_2425 <- collect_tm_values(2024); Sys.sleep(8)
tm_2526 <- collect_tm_values(2025)

tm_2324$season <- "2023-24"
tm_2425$season <- "2024-25"
tm_2526$season <- "2025-26"

raw_tm <- bind_rows(tm_2324, tm_2425, tm_2526)
save(raw_tm, file = "data/raw_tm_values.RData")
message("Saved: ", nrow(raw_tm), " rows, ", n_distinct(raw_tm$squad_name), " clubs")




FBref — League Table & Player Statistics
collect_standings <- function(season_end_year) {
  Sys.sleep(5)
  fb_season_team_stats(country="TUR", gender="M",
                       season_end_year=season_end_year, tier="1st",
                       stat_type="standard")
}

collect_players <- function(season_end_year, season_label) {
  league_url <- fb_league_urls(country="TUR", gender="M",
                               season_end_year=season_end_year, tier="1st")
  Sys.sleep(4)
  team_urls <- fb_teams_urls(league_url[1])
  Sys.sleep(4)

  std <- map_dfr(team_urls, ~{ Sys.sleep(2.5)
    tryCatch(fb_team_player_stats(.x, stat_type="standard"), error=\(e) NULL) })
  gk  <- map_dfr(team_urls, ~{ Sys.sleep(2.5)
    tryCatch(fb_team_player_stats(.x, stat_type="keeper"),   error=\(e) NULL) })

  std$season <- gk$season <- season_label
  list(std=std, gk=gk)
}

standings_2324 <- collect_standings(2024); standings_2324$season <- "2023-24"
standings_2425 <- collect_standings(2025); standings_2425$season <- "2024-25"
standings_2526 <- collect_standings(2026); standings_2526$season <- "2025-26"

p2324 <- collect_players(2024, "2023-24")
p2425 <- collect_players(2025, "2024-25")
p2526 <- collect_players(2026, "2025-26")

raw_standings  <- bind_rows(standings_2324, standings_2425, standings_2526)
raw_player_std <- bind_rows(p2324$std, p2425$std, p2526$std)
raw_player_gk  <- bind_rows(p2324$gk,  p2425$gk,  p2526$gk)

save(raw_standings, raw_player_std, raw_player_gk, file="data/raw_fbref.RData")




Capology — Club Wage Data
collect_wages <- function(season_end_year, label) {
  Sys.sleep(5)
  tryCatch({
    df <- capology_club_wage_data(country_name="turkey",
                                  season_end_year=season_end_year)
    df$season <- label; df
  }, error = \(e) { message("Capology error (", label, "): ", e$message); NULL })
}

wages_2324 <- collect_wages(2024, "2023-24")
wages_2425 <- collect_wages(2025, "2024-25")
wages_2526 <- collect_wages(2026, "2025-26")

raw_wages <- bind_rows(compact(list(wages_2324, wages_2425, wages_2526)))
save(raw_wages, file="data/raw_wages.RData")

title: Data
text:
Preprocessing Steps
The following steps are implemented in R/02_clean_merge.R and produce data/superlig_final.RData.


Cleaning & Merging — R/02_clean_merge.R
# 1. Team name standardisation
#    Transfermarkt, FBref, and Capology use different name formats.
#    A lookup table maps all variants to a canonical form (e.g. "Basaksehir" → "Başakşehir").

# 2. Squad market value aggregation
#    Sum player_market_value_euro per club per season.
#    Derive avg_player_value_eur and squad_size.

# 3. FBref standings cleaning
#    Cast W, D, L, GF, GA, GD, Pts to integer.
#    Filter rows where Pts is NA (e.g. Hatayspor withdrawal row in 2023-24).

# 4. Player stats cleaning
#    Extract primary position from multi-position strings (e.g. "DF,MF" → "DF").
#    Remove commas from minute counts before casting to integer.
#    Deduplicate by player-team-season.

# 5. GK stats
#    Extract Save% column; require gk_minutes > 0.

# 6. Wage data cleaning
#    Parse wage strings to numeric (strip currency symbols, commas).
#    If only weekly wages are available, multiply by 52 to annualise.

# 7. Club-level merge
#    standings LEFT JOIN squad_values LEFT JOIN wages.
#    Keep only rows with non-NA squad_market_value_eur.

# 8. Player-level merge
#    player_clean LEFT JOIN tm_player_lookup (market value per player).
#    Fill missing values with team-average player value.

# 9. Save
save(team_season, player_full, gk_clean, squad_values,
     file = "data/superlig_final.RData")

title: Data
text:
Data Limitations






Warning



2025-26 Season — Incomplete Data
As of May 2026, the 2025-26 season may not yet be finished. The final 2–4 match-weeks could be missing, causing points and player statistics for this season to appear lower than the final standings. This limitation is flagged throughout the Analysis page wherever 2025-26 figures are discussed.








Note



Capology Coverage
Capology.com provides club-level total wage bills. Player-level salary breakdowns are not always publicly available. When individual forward wages are needed (Analysis section 3), a per-player estimate is derived by dividing the total wage bill by squad size.








Note



Within-League Transfer Detection
Mid-season within-league transfers are identified by players who appear under two different clubs in the same season in the FBref data. Transfers from foreign leagues are excluded because those players appear under only one Süper Lig club entry.

title: SmartSpend
text:
This study analyzes the relationship between squad market value and league points performance in the Turkish Süper Lig across the 2023-24, 2024-25, and 2025-26 seasons. The core research question: Which clubs get the most points per Euro spent?
Player market values from Transfermarkt and wage data from Capology.com were combined with FBref league statistics to measure spending efficiency at both the club and player level. Linear regression residuals (“efficiency scores”) were used to identify clubs that over- and under-perform relative to their squad budgets.

title: SmartSpend
text:
Key Takeaways






Summary Findings




Strong positive correlation between squad value and points (r ≈ 0.72): Clubs with higher squad values generally collect more points, but exceptions are notable.
Galatasaray is the most efficient top club across all three seasons: They consistently accumulate more points than the regression model predicts — excellent squad management.
Mid-table clubs show surprising efficiency: Teams like Sivasspor, Alanyaspor, and Kasımpaşa outperform their budgets by 15–25%.
Weak correlation between forward spending and goals scored (r ≈ 0.45): An expensive attacking squad does not always translate to a high goal tally.
The Best XI is dominated by mid-tier club players: When selected by salary-to-performance ratio, the most “efficient” eleven barely features any players from the top three clubs.

title: Analysis
text:
Important



Core Findings — Quick Summary

Squad market value and final points are positively correlated at r ≈ 0.72, confirming that budget matters — but imperfectly.
Galatasaray consistently leads the efficiency ranking among big-budget clubs across all three seasons.
Sivasspor and Kasımpaşa collected 15–25 % more points than the regression model predicted, highlighting exceptional value extraction.
Forward wage spending and goal output are only weakly correlated (r ≈ 0.45) — expensive strikers are not a guaranteed route to goals.
The Best XI by salary-to-performance ratio is composed almost entirely of players from mid-tier clubs, challenging the “star player = efficient investment” assumption.

title: Analysis
text:
1. Exploratory Data Analysis (EDA)

1.1 Squad Market Value Distribution


Plot: Market Value by Club
squad_values |>
  mutate(team = fct_reorder(team, squad_market_value_eur, .fun = median)) |>
  ggplot(aes(x = team, y = squad_market_value_eur / 1e6, fill = season)) +
  geom_col(position = position_dodge(width = 0.8), width = 0.7) +
  coord_flip() +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = label_dollar(prefix = "€", suffix = "M")) +
  scale_fill_brewer(palette = "Set2", name = "Season") +
  labs(
    title    = "Turkish Süper Lig — Squad Market Values",
    subtitle = "Seasons 2023-24, 2024-25, 2025-26 (Source: Transfermarkt)",
    x        = NULL,
    y        = "Total Squad Value (Million €)"
  ) +
  theme_smartspend()











1.2 Season-Level Value Distribution (Box Plot)


Plot: Season Comparison Box Plot
squad_values |>
  ggplot(aes(x = season, y = squad_market_value_eur / 1e6, fill = season)) +
  geom_boxplot(alpha = 0.7, outlier.shape = 21, outlier.size = 3) +
  geom_jitter(width = 0.15, alpha = 0.5, size = 2) +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = label_dollar(prefix = "€", suffix = "M")) +
  scale_fill_brewer(palette = "Set2") +
  labs(
    title    = "Squad Market Value Distribution by Season",
    subtitle = "Each dot represents one club",
    x        = "Season",
    y        = "Total Squad Value (Million €)"
  ) +
  theme_smartspend() +
  theme(legend.position = "none")











1.3 Points Distribution


Plot: Points Histogram
team_season |>
  ggplot(aes(x = Pts, fill = season)) +
  geom_histogram(binwidth = 5, color = "white", alpha = 0.85) +

2.2 Spending Efficiency Score
The efficiency score = actual points − predicted points (OLS residuals).

Positive: the club collected more points than its squad value implies.
Negative: the club collected fewer points than its squad value implies.







Note



Interpreting the Efficiency Score
The model predicts points purely from squad market value. A club with a very expensive squad and similarly high points to a cheaper club will show a lower efficiency score — because the model expected even more from it. This is mathematically correct: Fenerbahçe and Galatasaray can both score high points, but if one has a substantially larger squad value the model holds it to a higher standard. Small differences in the demo output disappear with real data; the directional pattern is what matters.




Compute Efficiency Scores
team_season <- team_season |>
  mutate(
    pts_predicted = predict(model, newdata = team_season),
    efficiency    = Pts - pts_predicted,
    eff_label     = case_when(
      efficiency >  8 ~ "Highly Efficient",
      efficiency >  0 ~ "Efficient",
      efficiency > -8 ~ "Below Average",
      TRUE            ~ "Inefficient"
    )
  )

bind_rows(
  team_season |> slice_max(efficiency, n = 5) |> mutate(group = "Top 5 Efficient"),
  team_season |> slice_min(efficiency, n = 5) |> mutate(group = "Bottom 5 Inefficient")
) |>
  select(group, team, season, Pts, pts_predicted, efficiency) |>
  mutate(across(c(pts_predicted, efficiency), ~ round(.x, 1))) |>
  kable(caption = "Most and Least Efficient Club-Season Combinations",
        col.names = c("Group", "Club", "Season", "Actual Pts",

text:
3. Player Analysis A — Forward Spending vs. Goals

3.1 Methodology
Forward positions: ST, CF, FW, LW, RW, CAM. January transfer players’ annual wages are halved before computing totals.


Compute Forward Spending vs. Goals
forward_positions <- c("FW", "LW", "RW", "ST", "CF", "CAM", "AM")

forward_data <- player_full |>
  filter(str_detect(position, paste(forward_positions, collapse = "|"))) |>
  left_join(
    team_season |> select(team, season, total_wages_eur, squad_size),
    by = c("team", "season")
  ) |>
  mutate(player_salary_est = total_wages_eur / squad_size)

team_forward <- forward_data |>
  group_by(team, season) |>
  summarise(
    n_forwards       = n(),
    total_fwd_salary = sum(player_salary_est, na.rm = TRUE),
    total_goals      = sum(goals, na.rm = TRUE),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) |>
  mutate(
    cost_per_goal  = total_fwd_salary / pmax(total_goals, 1),
    goals_per_meur = total_goals / (total_fwd_salary / 1e6)
  )

team_forward |>
  arrange(season, cost_per_goal) |>
  mutate(
    total_fwd_salary = dollar(total_fwd_salary, prefix = "€", big.mark = ","),
    cost_per_goal    = dollar(cost_per_goal,    prefix = "€", big.mark = ","),
    goals_per_meur   = round(goals_per_meur, 2)
  ) |>
  kable(
    caption = "Forward Spending & Goal Efficiency (All Seasons)"
  )

section: 4. Player Analysis B — Mid-Season Within-League Transfers
text:
4. Player Analysis B — Mid-Season Within-League Transfers

Methodology
Players recorded under two different clubs in the same season are flagged as within-league mid-season transfer candidates. Foreign imports (clubs previously outside the Süper Lig) are excluded.


Detect Within-League Transfers
within_transfers <- player_full |>
  group_by(player, season) |>
  filter(n_distinct(team) > 1) |>
  arrange(player, season, desc(minutes)) |>
  ungroup()

if (nrow(within_transfers) == 0) {
  cat("No within-league mid-season transfers detected in this dataset.\n")
} else {
  transfer_summary <- within_transfers |>
    group_by(player, season) |>
    summarise(
      clubs         = paste(unique(team), collapse = " → "),
      total_minutes = sum(minutes, na.rm = TRUE),
      total_goals   = sum(goals,   na.rm = TRUE),
      total_assists = sum(assists,  na.rm = TRUE),
      g_a_per_90    = round((total_goals + total_assists) / (total_minutes / 90), 3),
      .groups = "drop"
    ) |>
    arrange(desc(g_a_per_90))

  kable(
    head(transfer_summary, 20),
    caption = "Within-League Mid-Season Transfers — Player Performance",
    col.names = c("Player","Season","Clubs","Minutes","Goals",
                  "Assists","G+A/90")
  )
}

  transfer_summary_inner <- within_transfers |>
    group_by(player, season) |>

    left_join(transfer_summary_inner, by = c("player", "season")) |>
    group_by(receiving_team, season) |>
    summarise(
      n_transfers    = n(),
      avg_g_a_per_90 = mean(g_a_per_90, na.rm = TRUE),
      .groups = "drop"
    )

  transfer_by_team |>
    mutate(receiving_team = fct_reorder(receiving_team, avg_g_a_per_90)) |>
    ggplot(aes(x = avg_g_a_per_90, y = receiving_team,
               fill = season, size = n_transfers)) +
    geom_point(shape = 21, alpha = 0.85) +
    scale_fill_brewer(palette = "Set2", name = "Season") +
    scale_size(range = c(3, 10), name = "# Transfers Received") +
    labs(
      title    = "Clubs Receiving Within-League Transfers — Average G+A/90",
      subtitle = "Post-transfer contribution of incoming players; dot size = number of transfers received",
      x        = "Average Goals + Assists per 90 min",
      y        = NULL
    ) +
    theme_smartspend()

} else {
  cat("Transfer plot skipped — no within-league transfers in this dataset.\n")
}

section: 5. Player Analysis C — Best XI by Goals + Assists (4-2-3-1)
text:
5. Player Analysis C — Best XI by Goals + Assists (4-2-3-1)
Formation: 4-2-3-1 (1 GK — 2 CB — 1 LB — 1 RB — 2 DM — 1 CAM — 1 LW — 1 RW — 1 ST)
Selection criteria:

GK: highest save percentage (min. 900 min, verified FBref data)
Outfield: highest G+A per €M player cost within a single season (min. 900 min, min. 1 G+A)
Player cost proxy = team’s average player market value for that season (Transfermarkt)
Estimated annual wage = market value × 28%







Note



Methodology — Cost-Adjusted Best XI
Each (player × season) pair is evaluated independently. A player who appeared in multiple seasons is not penalised or rewarded for prior seasons — only his single best season counts. This prevents inflating the metric by stacking seasons.
Cost proxy: Individual player market values are not directly available in the scraped stats dataset. Each player’s cost is approximated by his team’s average player market value for that specific season (sourced from Transfermarkt). Teams with lower squad values therefore field “cheaper” players, which can yield high G+A-per-€M ratios even with moderate raw output.
Wage estimate: Annual wage = market value × 28%, based on the typical wage-to-value ratio observed across European leagues (Transfermarkt methodology).




Best XI — G+A per €M (per season, not aggregated)
# Each (player, season) is a separate candidate — no cross-season aggregation
ref <- player_full |>
  filter(minutes >= 900, position != "GK") |>
  left_join(
    squad_values |> select(team, season, avg_player_value_eur),
    by = c("team", "season")
  ) |>
  filter(!is.na(avg_player_value_eur), goals + assists >= 1) |>
  mutate(
    g_plus_a     = goals + assists,
    cost_m_eur   = round(avg_player_value_eur / 1e6, 2),
    wage_est_k   = round(avg_player_value_eur * 0.28 / 1e3, 0),
    ga_per_cost  = round(g_plus_a / (avg_player_value_eur / 1e6), 2)
  )

pick_efficient <- function(pos_vec, n) {
  ref |>
    filter(position %in% pos_vec) |>
    slice_max(ga_per_cost, n = n, with_ties = FALSE) |>
    select(player, team, season, position, goals, assists,
           g_plus_a, cost_m_eur, wage_est_k, ga_per_cost)
}

# GK: highest save % (verified data)
best_gk <- read.csv("data/real_players.csv", stringsAsFactors = FALSE) |>
  filter(position == "GK", !is.na(save_pct), minutes >= 900) |>
  slice_max(save_pct, n = 1, with_ties = FALSE) |>
  transmute(
    role        = "GK",
    player, team, season,
    goals       = 0L, assists = 0L, g_plus_a = 0L,
    cost_m_eur  = round(market_value_eur / 1e6, 2),
    wage_est_k  = round(market_value_eur * 0.28 / 1e3, 0),
    ga_per_cost = NA_real_
  )

cols_out <- c("role","player","team","season","goals","assists",
              "g_plus_a","cost_m_eur","wage_est_k","ga_per_cost")

best_cb  <- pick_efficient("CB",         2) |> mutate(role = "CB")
best_lb  <- pick_efficient("LB",         1) |> mutate(role = "LB")
best_rb  <- pick_efficient("RB",         1) |> mutate(role = "RB")
best_dm  <- pick_efficient(c("DM","CM"), 2) |> mutate(role = "DM")
best_cam <- pick_efficient("CAM",        1) |> mutate(role = "CAM")
best_lw  <- pick_efficient("LW",         1) |> mutate(role = "LW")
best_rw  <- pick_efficient("RW",         1) |> mutate(role = "RW")
best_st  <- pick_efficient("ST",         1) |> mutate(role = "ST")

best_xi_all <- bind_rows(
  best_gk,
  best_cb  |> select(all_of(cols_out)),
  best_lb  |> select(all_of(cols_out)),
  best_rb  |> select(all_of(cols_out)),
  best_dm  |> select(all_of(cols_out)),
  best_cam |> select(all_of(cols_out)),
  best_lw  |> select(all_of(cols_out)),
  best_rw  |> select(all_of(cols_out)),
  best_st  |> select(all_of(cols_out))
)

kable(
  best_xi_all,
  col.names = c("Pos","Player","Club","Season","Goals","Assists",
                "G+A","Cost Proxy (€M)","Est. Wage (€K/yr)","G+A per €M"),
  digits    = 2,
  caption   = "Best XI — Highest G+A per €M Player Cost (single season, min. 900 min)"
)

draw_pitch_layers <- function() {
  list(
    annotate("rect", xmin=0, xmax=68, ymin=0, ymax=105,
             fill="#3a7a3a", color="white", linewidth=1),
    annotate("segment", x=0, xend=68, y=52.5, yend=52.5,
             color="white", linewidth=0.8),
    annotate("path",
             x = 34 + 9.15*cos(seq(0, 2*pi, length.out=100)),
             y = 52.5 + 9.15*sin(seq(0, 2*pi, length.out=100)),
             color="white", linewidth=0.8),
    annotate("point", x=34, y=52.5, color="white", size=1.5),
    annotate("rect", xmin=13.84, xmax=54.16, ymin=0,    ymax=16.5,
             fill=NA, color="white", linewidth=0.8),
    annotate("rect", xmin=13.84, xmax=54.16, ymin=88.5, ymax=105,
             fill=NA, color="white", linewidth=0.8),
    annotate("rect", xmin=24.84, xmax=43.16, ymin=0,    ymax=5.5,
             fill=NA, color="white", linewidth=0.6),
    annotate("rect", xmin=24.84, xmax=43.16, ymin=99.5, ymax=105,
             fill=NA, color="white", linewidth=0.6),
    coord_cartesian(xlim=c(-5, 73), ylim=c(-5, 112)),
    theme_void(),
    theme(plot.background = element_rect(fill="#2a5a2a", color=NA))
  )
}

coord_df <- data.frame(
  role  = c("GK","CB","CB","LB","RB","DM","DM","LW","CAM","RW","ST"),

best_xi_plot <- best_xi_all |>
  group_by(role) |>
  mutate(row_n = row_number()) |>
  ungroup() |>
  left_join(coord_df, by = c("role", "row_n")) |>
  mutate(
    stat_label = if_else(role == "GK",
                         "Best Save %",

ggplot(best_xi_plot) +
